findings.evidence: The route copies a RunIdSchema value directly into projectId. RunIdSchema allows a leading dash or underscore, while AiTeammateContractIdV1Schema requires the first character to be alphanumeric. makeRunId uses base64url, so valid generated run IDs can reach this mismatch. executeAiTeammateJobV1 parses the job and can throw before a terminal receipt exists; current route tests use only alphanumeric-leading IDs.
findings.scenario: A legitimate run whose ID begins with dash or underscore loads Agent Studio but proposal creation reaches an unhandled server failure and the UI wrongly blames the assignment.
findings.whyItMatters: A valid subset of application runs cannot use the feature, the failure is misattributed, and the terminal-receipt invariant is bypassed before the executor can bind a receipt.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Construct a grammar-safe projectId or safe-parse the constructed job and return a stable JSON response; test valid dash- and underscore-leading run IDs.

findings.evidence: AgentStudioPanel is rendered only while the assistant tool is active and is replaced in View mode. Assignment, result, and request-generation state live inside the unmounted subtree. Ordinary Canvas selection changes activeTool to text or selection, so an in-flight result is discarded and typed assignment or process-only receipt is lost. The persistent composer was separately hoisted to survive tool changes.
findings.scenario: A user writes an assignment or receives a receipt, then clicks the preview element they are discussing. Canvas changes tools and remounting Agent Studio returns an empty form with no recoverable receipt.
findings.whyItMatters: Routine Canvas interaction silently destroys the local work product and contradicts the intended selection-continuity model.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Keep AgentStudioPanel mounted after first open and hide it when inactive, or otherwise hoist its local state within authorized paths; add a state-continuity oracle. Narrow documentation to the continuity actually guaranteed.

findings.evidence: The route returns a fixed deterministic template, but the UI announces a named teammate as Working, says a proposal is being created, labels the result Proposal, and attributes it as Proposed by the teammate. Local foundation appears only as a badge; no visible sentence says no model/provider is connected or that the result is a fixed placeholder.
findings.scenario: A user submits a detailed SEO assignment and reasonably believes the named teammate reviewed it, even though the result is a constant contract-proving sentence.
findings.whyItMatters: The selected specification explicitly forbids implying a provider-backed agent is connected; the current attribution does exactly that despite an otherwise sound read/propose boundary.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Add an explicit no-model/no-provider disclosure, label the output Placeholder proposal or equivalent, and keep roster availability truthfully static while the form live region reports request progress; assert the disclosure in component and Canvas contracts.

findings.evidence: The route may validly return HTTP 200 with proposal null and a rejected, failed, cancelled, or budget-exhausted receipt. The client accepts only complete plus proposal and otherwise reports an invalid receipt, advises retry, hides the valid receipt, and marks the assignment textarea invalid regardless of failure source. A canonicalized input can exceed the executor byte budget while staying inside the textarea character limit.
findings.scenario: A bounded assignment containing many escaped control characters correctly produces a budget-exhausted receipt, but the pane calls it invalid, flags the text field, and hides the terminal outcome.
findings.whyItMatters: The message and retry advice are false, and four of the five specified terminal states cannot be represented by Canvas.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Represent valid non-complete receipts as a distinct terminal result, render status and stopping condition without false retry advice, and reserve aria-invalid for local field validation; add route and component coverage.

findings.evidence: AgentStudioPanel receives selection but forwards it only to Site Advice. Teammates shows neither a selection scope nor a disclaimer, while the selection breadcrumb and persistent composer selection chip surround it. The teammate job contains only task text and carries no editId.
findings.scenario: With hero.headline selected, a user asks a teammate to make this punchier and reasonably assumes the live selection is part of the assignment, although it is not sent or recorded.
findings.whyItMatters: Selection scopes the next prompt elsewhere in the approved Canvas model, making Teammates the one ambiguous exception.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Pass selection for display only and state that the local assignment does not carry the current element reference. Do not add editId to the closed job contract in this slice.

findings.evidence: The Data class select offers Project internal and Public without a persistent description. The value is only a caller assertion, not content scanning or project access, but the UI never says so. The user is not warned not to paste credentials, cookies, client-sensitive, release, or appointment data.
findings.scenario: A user selects Project internal and pastes sensitive client content, believing the label both grants project context and enforces classification.
findings.whyItMatters: The boundary depends on user restraint, while the current control implies powers and enforcement the slice does not have.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Add persistent descriptive safety copy, bind it to the select with aria-describedby, clarify that nothing is scanned or read from the project, and assert it in component and Canvas contracts.

findings.evidence: Component tests use static markup and pure helpers. The Agent Studio E2E surface uses pointer-style check, fill, and click APIs; it contains no keyboard.press path. Source and CSS substring assertions do not prove real keyboard operation, focus visibility, busy locking, or stale-result behavior under real events.
findings.scenario: A regression in radio arrow navigation, keyboard submit, or live busy locking can pass every current test while acceptance criterion 5 still claims keyboard proof.
findings.whyItMatters: The specification requires keyboard operation and visible focus, but current proof is mostly semantic markup rather than behavior.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Add a real keyboard path to the existing Canvas E2E and assert focus placement/visibility plus working-state locking. Do not add a runtime or test dependency merely for this slice.

findings.evidence: The focused submit control becomes disabled during submission and the component does not intentionally move focus to the result or restore it when the button re-enables.
findings.scenario: A keyboard user activates Create proposal and may lose a coherent focus position while the result is announced, making the next keyboard action unpredictable.
findings.whyItMatters: The slice promises keyboard operation and visible focus, but submit-to-result focus behavior is neither designed nor tested.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Keep the submit control focusable with aria-disabled plus the existing synchronous guard, or intentionally focus the result heading after a committed result; prove the chosen behavior with a keyboard assertion.

overreachAssessment: The implementation does not expose apply, provider calls, browser, persistence, scheduling, memory, collaboration, deployment, or release and stays within the read/propose effect boundary. The overreach is presentational: a UI-invented Working lifecycle and Proposed by attribution make a fixed deterministic template feel like a connected teammate. Three natural-language surfaces remain distinct but crowded; the smallest correction is to clarify scope, data handling, and placeholder status rather than remove the panel.
underreachAssessment: Inside the authorized slice, the material underreach is represented by F-01, F-02, F-04, F-05, F-06, F-07, and F-08: edge-run correctness, state continuity, terminal-receipt rendering, selection disclosure, data-class semantics, and real keyboard/focus proof. Explicit future capabilities are not counted as underreach.
duplicationAssessment: Agent Studio Teammates, Site Advice, and the persistent composer are three adjacent natural-language surfaces. Source inspection found distinct responsibilities: deterministic teammate proposal, legacy site advice/apply, and selection-scoped edit/apply. No control should be removed in this slice; F-03, F-05, and F-06 provide the minimum disambiguation needed to prevent perceived duplication.
authorityDriftAssessment: No implemented provider, network, credential, filesystem, shell, browser, mutate, external-effect, authority, background-process, persistent-storage, Deep Agents, LangGraph, LangSmith, deployment, or release capability was found. All eight corrections were classified inside the current exact paths/effects; adding selection to the job payload, real model work, durable history, or any future capability remains outside the correction cage.
deferredScopeAssessment: Blocked A4 motion, the draft operating environment, embedded browser, collaboration/presence, provider and model routing, skills, memory, scheduled/background tasks, persistent proposal history, Page IR mutation, deployment, and release remain explicitly deferred. Residual risks that would require those capabilities are recorded but do not authorize implementation and were not scored as defects merely because they are absent.
